toolCalls.name: bash
toolCalls.argsSummary: bash command=pwd && ls -la && echo "---" && ls -R src 2>/dev/null | head -50

session.assistantText:
Restating the goal: a read-only explorer reads the `src` directory and reports what each file does, without modifying anything.

Only DeepSeek/magpie routes exist in this deployment, so the "code and judgment" default of `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh-fast` is unavailable. I will run the explorer on the inherited parent route (`magpie/workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash`, effort `high`) and say so.
The read-only explorer finished. Nothing was modified.

**Files under `src/`**

- [src/a.ts](src/a.ts) — one line, exports `const a = 1`. Placeholder value module, no imports, no behavior.
- [src/b.ts](src/b.ts) — one line, exports `const b = 2`. Placeholder value module, no imports, no behavior.

**Relationship** — the two files are fully independent. Neither imports the other or anything else, so there is no runtime or type coupling. They are scaffold placeholders, one constant per file. Because each `const` is literal-typed, an importer gets the narrowest type possible, and the files could be merged or renamed without touching a caller.

`README.md` holds a single line, `# 只读探查` ("read-only exploration"), confirming this workspace exists to exercise a read-only probe rather than real logic.

Two notes on how this ran. The explorer ran on the `readonly` preset, so its sandbox was read-only and no write was possible, matching your constraint. The pstack default model for code and judgment is `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh-fast`, which this deployment does not serve. Available routes are DeepSeek Account (`deepseek-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`) and magpie (`workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash`), so the child inherited the parent route, `magpie/workbuddy/minimax-m3.1-flash` at `high` effort. If you want the report re-run on a different model, say which and I will spawn a fresh explorer with that route.
